title: OmniGet: Your New Dev Superpower for Downloads and Media Mastery!
contentMarkdown:
## 📝 Quick Summary: 
OmniGet is a free, open-source desktop application for Windows, macOS, and Linux that simplifies downloading media from over 1,800 websites, including Udemy, Hotmart, and YouTube. It integrates a media player, EPUB reader, and music library, all powered by yt-dlp, ensuring user files remain on their local computer.

## 🔑 Key Takeaways

- ✅ OmniGet is a free, open-source desktop app for Windows, macOS, and Linux, acting as an all-in-one media downloader and toolbox.

- ✅ It supports downloading content from over 1,800 sites, including popular platforms like YouTube, Instagram, X, TikTok, and crucial learning sites like Udemy and Hotmart.

- ✅ Beyond downloads, it offers a suite of tools including Whisper transcription, media conversion, EPUB/PDF reading, and Anki flashcard creation for comprehensive media management.

- ✅ The project prioritizes user privacy with no accounts, ads, or telemetry, ensuring your files and data remain on your local machine.

- ✅ Built with modern tech (Tauri, Rust, Svelte), OmniGet significantly boosts productivity by consolidating multiple media-related tasks into a single, user-friendly application.


## 📊 Project Statistics
- ⭐ Stars: 12156
- 🍴 Forks: 1050
- ❗ Open Issues: 32


## 🛠 Tech Stack
- ✅ Rust


Hey fellow developers! Ever feel like you're juggling a dozen different tools just to download a YouTube video, grab a course from Udemy, or save a cool Instagram reel? What if I told you there's a single, elegant desktop application that handles all of that, and then some? Get ready to say hello to OmniGet, a GitHub project that's quickly becoming my go-to for all things media!

OmniGet isn't just another downloader; it's a full-blown media toolbox packed into one free, open-source app for Windows, macOS, and Linux. Imagine pasting a link from virtually anywhere – be it YouTube, Instagram, X (Twitter), Pinterest, TikTok, Reddit, Twitch, Bilibili, Telegram, or even major course platforms like Udemy and Hotmart – and OmniGet just... gets it. It's essentially a user-friendly graphical interface built on top of the incredibly powerful yt-dlp, making all that command-line magic accessible with a click.

But here's where it gets really exciting: OmniGet goes way beyond simple downloads. It's truly an 'omni' tool. Need to transcribe audio from a downloaded video? It's got Whisper transcription built-in. Want to convert a video format? Yep. It even includes an EPUB and PDF reader, a music player, and tools for creating Anki flashcards for spaced repetition. Think about that for a second – you can download a course, transcribe its lectures, convert materials, and then use the app to study them! This is a game-changer for anyone who learns online or wants to keep their digital media organized and accessible.

The benefits for us developers are huge. First, it's a massive productivity booster. No more switching between browser extensions, command-line scripts, and separate media players. Everything is consolidated. Second, it's completely privacy-focused. There are no accounts, no ads, and absolutely no telemetry on what you download. Your files stay on your computer, period. This is a big win in an age where data privacy is paramount. Plus, being open source under the GPL-3.0 license means you can inspect the code, contribute, or just trust that it's doing what it says.

OmniGet is built with modern technologies like Tauri, Rust, and Svelte, ensuring a performant and responsive user experience. It's already garnered over 9,500 stars on GitHub and is the most starred project in the `udemy-downloader`, `hotmart-downloader`, and `course-downloader` topics – a testament to its quality and utility. If you're looking to streamline your media workflow, gain control over your digital content, and support an awesome open-source project, you absolutely need to check out OmniGet. It's a true gem that makes managing your digital life so much easier!
